#1948: the monolithic "Test front" step was renamed to "Test front (non-vitest)" and now runs only the non-vitest checks (pnpm --filter front test:ci-non-vitest). The vitest suite moved out into its own 4-way shard matrix job (test-vitest, run via --shard=i/4) plus a parallel coverage-equality job (test-vitest-coverage), so no verification work was dropped — the split is what makes shard failures report independently instead of masking later steps (#1699). The replacement steps are reconciled as new manifest entries in the same commit.

steps.step_id: require-linked-issue.yml::require-linked-issue::Verify the PR closes an existing issue
steps.reason: #2003: renamed to "Verify the PR links an existing issue" because the guard now accepts explicit non-closing relationships for honest partial slices as well as closing keywords. The replacement step keeps real-issue validation and pull-request rejection; no verification was removed.

#2049 / owner-approved guard-pruning policy tracked by #2068: the PR-body prose parser, its tests, and this checkout are retired. A sound replacement would require a Markdown and natural-language analyzer disproportionate to this non-runtime policy, so the guard is dropped rather than rebuilt. Honest disclosure: genuine unenumerated or quantified PR-body claims will no longer be rejected automatically — human review owns this check after retirement. The separate require-linked-issue job remains intact and unaffected.

steps.step_id: require-linked-issue.yml::pr-body-exhaustiveness::Verify the PR body makes no unverifiable exhaustiveness claims (#1569)
steps.reason: #2049 / owner-approved guard-pruning policy tracked by #2068: this lexical PR-prose check cannot distinguish an assertion from a quotation, retraction, result, or hypothesis; rebuilding it correctly would require a Markdown and natural-language analyzer disproportionate to this non-runtime policy, so the guard is retired instead of patched. Honest disclosure: the automatic enforcement of evidence-backed, exhaustive PR-body claims is lost — genuine unenumerated or quantified claims will no longer be rejected automatically, and human review owns this check after retirement. No runtime, security, data, API, supply-chain, or CI-integrity invariant is lost; the lost invariant is review-process policy only.
